change.before: "SHA-256 always used when signing with RSA"
change.after: "3072-bit keys use SHA-384, 4096-bit keys use SHA-512"

exposure.needed: whether cert-manager signs with RSA keys of 3072 or 4096 bits (e.g. CA or self-signed issuer keys held in Secrets)

consequence.statement: RSA certificates with 3072-bit and 4096-bit keys will use SHA-384 and SHA-512 respectively for signature hashing instead of SHA-256, which may affect compatibility with systems that do not support these stronger hash algorithms, though the evidence indicates minimal impact on standard Kubernetes environments.
consequence.remediation: Verify that systems consuming these certificates support SHA-384 and SHA-512 hashing algorithms if you are using RSA keys larger than 2048-bit.

evidence.excerpt:
### RSA Certificate Compliance

The United States Department of Defense published a [memo: Department of Defense Transition to Stronger Public Key Infrastructure Algorithms](https://dl.dod.cyber.mil/wp-content/uploads/pki-pke/pdf/unclass-memo_dodcryptoalgorithms.pdf) in 2022 which introduced some requirements on the kinds of cryptography they require to be supported in software they use.

In effect, the memo requires that software be able to support larger RSA keys (3072-bit and 4096-bit) and hashing algorithms (SHA-384 at a minimum).

cert-manager supported large RSA keys long before the memo…
